newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Woman plans global helicopter trip for HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Woman plans global helicopter trip for HK handover.

text.p: A Hong Kong resident said on Wednesday she planned to mark the British colony's handover to China with the first ever round-the-world helicopter flight by a woman.

Jennifer Murray, 56, told Reuters that she planned to take off from London on May 10 in a light Robinson R44 helicopter on a three-month odyssey that will take her through Europe, the Middle East, Asia and North America.
She will arrive in Hong Kong, her home for 30 years, in late June. The territory is due to be handed back to China at midnight on June 30.
"This will probably be the biggest event in my lifetime. I can't see anything that is going to eclipse this one," she said.
Murray and her husband Simon, chairman of Deutsche Bank Asia, have long been prominent figures in Hong Kong.
She believes her trip, with British co-pilot Quentin Smith, will be only the fourth round-the-world flight by helicopter and the first by a woman, and the first by anyone in such a light model.
Sponsored by British Petroleum which will help provide fuel, Murray said she hoped to donate any money raised to the global Save The Children charity.
